title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.263): X is a germ of differentiable surface at x. V = T_x X, and S_x = (V\{0})/R_{>0} is the circle of tangent directions. D_x^* is the punctured germ at x. A_x is the poset of proper arcs of S_x. For an arc A, E_p(A) is the corresponding germ of sector in D_x^*. Universal coverings S~_x → S_x and D_x^{*~} → D_x^* have been chosen. The goal is an axiomatic, canonical version of the bijection (95) between 'relèvements' to the two universal coverings.

(97) Fix an arc A. Since A is contractible, the set S~_x(A) := Γ(A, S~_x/S_x) of sections of the covering over A is a torsor under the deck group π_1(S_x) ≅ Z. Likewise, D_x^{*~}(E_p(A)) := Γ(E_p(A), D_x^{*~}/D_x^*), the sections over the germ of sector, is a torsor under π_1(D_x^*) ≅ Z. Both deck groups are identified canonically with T_x, the Z-module of orientations of X at x; an orientation of V orients both the circle of directions and the small loops around x.

(98) H(A) = Isom_{T_x}(S~_x(A), D_x^{*~}(E_p(A))). Since T_x is abelian, this is again a T_x-torsor.

(99)–(100) For A ⊂ A', restriction gives torsor isomorphisms S~(A') → S~(A) and D~(E_p(A')) → D~(E_p(A)). Conjugating by these gives H(A) ≅ H(A').

(101) So H is a functor from the order category A_x to Tors(T_x). Every arrow of the target is invertible, so H factors through the groupoid Gr(A_x) obtained by inverting all arrows (102).

Next page: Gr(A_x) is equivalent to the groupoid of universal covers of S_x (it is the fundamental groupoid of the circle, equivalently of the nerve of the arc poset). The key claim is that Gr(H) is essentially constant. Following the generator loop multiplies both torsors by the same element of T_x, so the induced action on Isom is trivial. Hence the H(A) are linked by a transitive system of isomorphisms. Their common value H(S~_x, D~_x^*) is a canonical T_x-torsor that depends only on the chosen universal covers.

In modern terms, this is an abstract version of the canonical identification π_1(S_x) ≅ π_1(D_x^*) obtained from the oriented real blow-up at x: the boundary circle of directions is homotopic to the punctured neighbourhood. It is the topological core of 'tangential base points', made sector-by-sector and functorial in the arcs.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. One minor point: (99) as written gives restriction maps from A' to A, so the isomorphism (100) H(A) → H(A') is obtained by conjugation/inversion. Variance is harmless because everything is invertible.
Sections over E_p(A) must be read in the germ sense (a filter of neighbourhoods / pro-object), as the p.263 margin indicates. The page leaves this implicit.

ideas.what: Torsors of sections of universal covers over contractible arcs and sectors, under the orientation module T_x
ideas.modern_name: Deck-transformation torsors; orientation sheaf identification π_1(S^1) ≅ or_x

ideas.what: H(A) = Isom of two T_x-torsors, functorial in the arc poset, factoring through the groupoid localization Gr(A_x)

ideas.what: Essential constancy (trivial monodromy) giving a canonical torsor H(S~_x, D~_x^*) comparing the universal covers of the direction circle and of the punctured germ

missed.claim: A sector-by-sector, functorial axiomatization of the comparison between the circle of tangent directions and the punctured germ. It is built as a torsor of isomorphisms over the poset of arcs, part of a 'Teichmüller groupoid' formalism for surfaces in the Longue Marche sequel. It is a pedagogically clean, unpublished formalization rather than a new result.
missed.quote: H(A) = Isom_{T_x}(S~_x(A), D_x^{*~}(E_p(A))) qui est lui-même un T_x-torseur
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an explicit combinatorial model of tangential base points via arcs and sectors. It may interest people formalizing Teichmüller groupoids and tangential basepoints combinatorially (e.g. the Grothendieck–Teichmüller tower), but the content is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful, routine topology (an orientation-torsor comparison with trivial monodromy) supporting the tangential-base-point setup. The specific arc-poset/torsor-of-Isom formalism is unpublished but would not surprise a specialist.

'groupoïde associé W[?]' — the 'W' looks like a stray mark or insertion; likely just 'groupoïde associé Gr(A_x)'.
